medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually (BP, renal function, potassium)
medications.purpose: First‑line antihypertensive to achieve target <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑inhibitor as first‑line for non‑Afro‑Caribbean adults <55 y

medications.dose: 1 g orally every 6 h as needed (max 4 g/24 h)
medications.purpose: Replace naproxen to avoid NSAID‑induced BP elevation and renal risk
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises avoiding NSAIDs in hypertension where possible

interactions_checked.interaction: NSAIDs can blunt the antihypertensive effect of ACE‑I and increase risk of acute kidney injury and hyperkalaemia
interactions_checked.action: Obtain baseline eGFR and potassium before starting Ramipril; repeat labs 1–2 weeks after initiation and after any dose change; advise patient to switch from naproxen to paracetamol or topical NSAID

contraindications.reason: No added benefit and increased renal risk per NICE NG136
contraindications.alternative: Use either an ACE‑I (ramipril) or an ARB (candesartan) if ACE‑I intolerant

contraindications.drug: High‑dose thiazide diuretic (>12.5 mg chlortalidone or >2.5 mg bendroflumethiazide)
contraindications.reason: May worsen glucose tolerance and dyslipidaemia in metabolic‑syndrome patients (NG136)
contraindications.alternative: Low‑dose indapamide MR 1.5 mg if additional BP control needed

contraindications.reason: Not recommended as first‑line; may impair glucose tolerance (NG136)
contraindications.alternative: Reserve beta‑blocker for heart‑failure or post‑MI indications

assumptions_warnings: eGFR, serum creatinine and potassium are not available – assumed normal for ACE‑I initiation; labs must be obtained before and after starting ramipril
QRISK score not calculated – required by NG136 to determine need for statin therapy; obtain lipid profile and calculate QRISK
Liver function tests not available – required before any future statin prescription
Allergy status unknown – must confirm no ACE‑I or sulfonamide allergy
Ethnicity not recorded – if patient is Afro‑Caribbean, calcium‑channel blocker (amlodipine) would be preferred first‑line
Pregnancy intention unknown – ACE‑I contraindicated in pregnancy; ensure effective contraception if ramipril prescribed
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily as first‑line therapy for hypertension per NICE NG136, with titration to 5 mg then 10 mg as tolerated to reach BP <140/90 mmHg. Replace systemic naproxen with paracetamol to avoid NSAID‑related BP elevation and renal risk. Obtain baseline renal function, electrolytes, LFTs, lipid profile and calculate QRISK before any further pharmacologic interventions (e.g., statin, additional antihypertensives). Monitor BP, renal function and potassium at 2 weeks, then regularly; review medication annually.
